title: CNS / Glioma Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides. Adult diffuse glioma pathway: workup -> maximal safe resection / biopsy -> WHO 2021 molecular class (IDH, 1p/19q) -> grade and risk stratification -> subtype-directed local (surgery/RT) and systemic therapy -> surveillance -> recurrence. No CNS-specific dose protocol exists in the StewardMD protocol library yet, so systemic-therapy leaves are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose; the physician arranges the regimen. No proprietary guideline text reproduced.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (NCCN CNS, DeVita, Harrison) and WHO CNS5 (2021) molecular classification. Content authored in original wording; invents no dose or regimen.

a.text: Stupp-type regimen: maximal safe resection followed by focal radiation with concurrent daily temozolomide, then adjuvant temozolomide cycles. Alternating electric-field therapy (TTFields) may be added in the adjuvant phase for supratentorial glioblastoma.

b.text: PCV = procarbazine, lomustine (CCNU), vincristine. Radiation followed by PCV is a standard chemoradiation backbone for 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma; some centers substitute temozolomide for tolerability.

c.text: Higher-risk lower-grade glioma is generally taken as age over ~40 or subtotal resection / residual disease (also large tumor, neurologic deficit, high proliferation). Such patients are offered postoperative radiation plus chemotherapy rather than observation.

d.text: MGMT promoter methylation predicts benefit from alkylating chemotherapy and is most decision-relevant in elderly / frailer glioblastoma, where it helps choose between temozolomide-containing therapy and radiation alone. It is prognostic but does not withhold Stupp therapy in fit patients.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and tissue diagnosis
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation of a suspected diffuse glioma before definitive management.

bullets.label: Contrast MRI brain (structural)
bullets.sub: consider perfusion / spectroscopy; MR is the reference imaging

bullets.label: Tissue diagnosis by maximal safe resection or biopsy
Molecular testing: IDH1/2 mutation, 1p/19q codeletion, ATRX, MGMT promoter methylation
bullets.sub: add CDKN2A/B, EGFR, +7/-10, TERT for grading of IDH-wildtype tumors

bullets.label: Perioperative supportive care
bullets.sub: corticosteroids for symptomatic edema, anti-seizure medication only if seizures, VTE awareness

bullets.label: Multidisciplinary review (neurosurgery, neuro-oncology, radiation oncology, neuropathology)

nodes.name: Clinical setting
nodes.title: Clinical setting
nodes.description: Choose the current scenario. Management branches by whether this is a new diagnosis, routine surveillance, or recurrence.

nodes.name: Resection
nodes.title: Maximal safe resection / biopsy
nodes.description: Extent of resection is both diagnostic and prognostic. Greater resection improves outcome when it can be achieved safely; otherwise biopsy secures the integrated diagnosis.
bullets: Aim for maximal safe cytoreduction within functional limits (awake mapping / intraoperative adjuncts as indicated)
Send tissue for integrated histologic + molecular classification
Extent of resection recorded (gross-total, subtotal, biopsy) - feeds risk stratification

nodes.name: Molecular class
nodes.title: WHO 2021 molecular class (IDH / 1p-19q)
nodes.description: Adult diffuse gliomas are classified first by IDH status and 1p/19q codeletion, which define three lineages and drive treatment more than histology alone.

bullets.label: Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant
bullets.sub: IDH-mutant, 1p/19q intact (grade 2, 3, or 4; CDKN2A/B loss upgrades to grade 4)

bullets.label: Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype
bullets.sub: IDH-wildtype with molecular GBM features: EGFR amplification, +7/-10, or TERT promoter mutation (grade 4)

tables.title: WHO CNS5 adult diffuse glioma classes

nodes.name: Await molecular
nodes.title: Molecular pending: defer adjuvant, optimize recovery
nodes.description: Integrated diagnosis not yet complete. Adjuvant therapy choice depends on IDH / 1p-19q, so defer it until results return.
bullets: Complete IDH, 1p/19q, MGMT, and grading markers before committing to adjuvant therapy
Continue supportive care; taper steroids as edema allows
Re-enter the class pathway once the integrated diagnosis is available
Do not start radiation or chemotherapy on histology alone if molecular results are imminent

nodes.name: Oligo grade
nodes.title: Oligodendroglioma: grade
nodes.description: Codeleted oligodendroglioma is graded 2 (lower-grade) or 3 (anaplastic). Grade and risk drive whether chemoradiation follows surgery.

nodes.name: Oligo G2 risk
nodes.title: Grade 2 oligodendroglioma: risk group
nodes.description: Lower-grade glioma is split into lower-risk (candidate for observation) and higher-risk (postoperative chemoradiation).

bullets.label: Lower-risk
bullets.sub: younger (about <= 40) AND gross-total / near-total resection, minimal residual, no major deficit

bullets.label: Higher-risk
bullets.sub: age > 40, OR subtotal resection / residual disease, OR large tumor / neurologic deficit

nodes.name: Oligo G2 observe
nodes.title: Grade 2 oligodendroglioma, lower-risk: resection + observation
nodes.description: After maximal safe resection, close MRI observation is reasonable for lower-risk codeleted grade 2 disease, reserving radiation and chemotherapy for progression.
bullets: Maximal safe resection is the primary treatment
Serial MRI surveillance (for example every 3-6 months initially, then lengthen)
Defer radiation + PCV to documented progression or reclassification to higher-risk
Manage seizures; support neurocognition

nodes.name: Oligo G2 chemoRT
nodes.title: Grade 2 oligodendroglioma, higher-risk: RT + PCV
nodes.description: Higher-risk codeleted grade 2 disease benefits from postoperative radiation followed by chemotherapy.
bullets: Focal external-beam radiation to the tumor bed
Followed by PCV (procarbazine, lomustine, vincristine); temozolomide is an alternative backbone at some centers
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the regimen (guidance only, no dose here)
Baseline and serial neurocognitive assessment

nodes.name: Oligo G3 chemoRT
nodes.title: Grade 3 oligodendroglioma (anaplastic): RT + PCV
nodes.description: Anaplastic codeleted oligodendroglioma is treated with radiation plus chemotherapy after maximal safe resection - the codeletion predicts strong chemotherapy benefit.
bullets: Maximal safe resection, then focal radiation
Chemotherapy with PCV (preferred by long-term data); temozolomide is an alternative
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the regimen (guidance only, no dose here)
Surveillance MRI after completion

nodes.name: Astro grade
nodes.title: Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant: grade
nodes.description: IDH-mutant astrocytoma is graded 2, 3, or 4 (CDKN2A/B homozygous loss defines grade 4). Grade drives the intensity of postoperative therapy.

nodes.name: Astro G2 risk
nodes.title: Grade 2 IDH-mutant astrocytoma: risk group
nodes.description: As with oligodendroglioma, lower-risk grade 2 astrocytoma may be observed after resection while higher-risk disease gets postoperative chemoradiation.

bullets.label: Higher-risk
bullets.sub: age > 40, or residual disease after subtotal resection / biopsy

nodes.name: Astro G2 observe
nodes.title: Grade 2 IDH-mut astrocytoma, lower-risk: resection + observation
nodes.description: Maximal safe resection with MRI surveillance is reasonable for lower-risk grade 2 IDH-mutant astrocytoma.
bullets: Maximal safe resection is primary therapy
Serial MRI surveillance; reserve radiation + temozolomide for progression or reclassification
Manage seizures; support neurocognition

nodes.name: Astro G2 chemoRT
nodes.title: Grade 2 IDH-mut astrocytoma, higher-risk: RT + temozolomide
nodes.description: Higher-risk grade 2 IDH-mutant astrocytoma is treated with postoperative radiation followed by alkylating chemotherapy.
bullets: Focal radiation to the tumor bed
Followed by alkylating chemotherapy (temozolomide; PCV is an alternative)
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the regimen (guidance only, no dose here)
Serial neurocognitive assessment

nodes.name: Astro G3 chemoRT
nodes.title: Grade 3 IDH-mut astrocytoma (anaplastic): RT + temozolomide
nodes.description: Anaplastic IDH-mutant astrocytoma is treated with radiation plus temozolomide after maximal safe resection.
bullets: Maximal safe resection, then focal radiation
Temozolomide (concurrent and/or adjuvant); PCV is an alternative alkylator backbone
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the regimen (guidance only, no dose here)
Surveillance MRI after completion

nodes.name: Astro G4 chemoRT
nodes.title: Grade 4 IDH-mut astrocytoma: RT + temozolomide (Stupp-type)
nodes.description: Grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma is treated like glioblastoma with a Stupp-type chemoradiation backbone, recognizing its more favorable biology than IDH-wildtype GBM.
bullets: Maximal safe resection, then focal radiation with concurrent then adjuvant temozolomide
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the Stupp-type regimen (guidance only, no dose here)
Surveillance MRI after completion

nodes.name: GBM fitness
nodes.title: Glioblastoma: age / performance status
nodes.description: In IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, age and performance status choose between full Stupp therapy and an abbreviated elderly / frail regimen.

bullets.label: Fit
bullets.sub: younger / good performance status (e.g. KPS >= 70), able to tolerate full chemoradiation

nodes.name: GBM Stupp
nodes.title: Glioblastoma, fit: Stupp chemoradiation (+/- TTFields)
nodes.description: Standard of care for fit IDH-wildtype glioblastoma is maximal safe resection followed by concurrent chemoradiation and adjuvant temozolomide, given regardless of MGMT status.
bullets: Maximal safe resection
Focal radiation with concurrent daily temozolomide, then adjuvant temozolomide cycles
Consider adding TTFields (alternating electric fields) in the adjuvant phase for supratentorial disease
MGMT methylation is prognostic but does not withhold Stupp therapy in fit patients
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the Stupp regimen (guidance only, no dose here)

nodes.name: GBM elderly MGMT
nodes.title: Elderly / frail glioblastoma: MGMT status
nodes.description: In the elderly / frail glioblastoma, MGMT promoter methylation guides whether to use temozolomide-containing therapy or radiation alone with a hypofractionated schedule.

nodes.name: GBM elderly TMZ
nodes.title: Elderly GBM, MGMT methylated: hypofractionated RT + temozolomide
nodes.description: Methylated elderly glioblastoma benefits most from an alkylating agent; a hypofractionated radiation course with temozolomide (or temozolomide alone if radiation is not tolerable) is preferred.
bullets: Hypofractionated (short-course) radiation with concurrent / adjuvant temozolomide
Temozolomide alone is an option if radiation is not feasible (methylated tumors respond)
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the regimen (guidance only, no dose here)
Attention to marrow tolerance and performance status

nodes.name: GBM elderly chemoRT
nodes.title: Elderly GBM, MGMT unknown: hypofractionated RT + temozolomide
nodes.description: When MGMT status is unavailable, a hypofractionated radiation course with temozolomide is a pragmatic default for the elderly patient who can tolerate combined therapy.
bullets: Hypofractionated radiation with concurrent / adjuvant temozolomide
Send MGMT if not already done to refine the choice
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the regimen (guidance only, no dose here)

nodes.name: GBM elderly RT
nodes.title: Elderly GBM, MGMT unmethylated: hypofractionated RT alone
nodes.description: Unmethylated elderly glioblastoma derives little from temozolomide; hypofractionated radiation alone is a reasonable, better-tolerated choice, with best supportive care for the frailest.
bullets: Hypofractionated radiation alone
Best supportive care for the frailest / lowest performance status
Adding temozolomide gives limited benefit in unmethylated tumors
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the regimen (guidance only, no dose here)

nodes.name: Surveillance type
nodes.title: Surveillance: tumor grade
nodes.description: Follow-up cadence differs by grade. Choose the treated tumor category.

nodes.name: LGG surveillance
nodes.title: Lower-grade glioma surveillance
nodes.description: Long-horizon MRI surveillance, since lower-grade gliomas progress slowly and can transform.
bullets: MRI at intervals (for example every 3-6 months for 5 years, then lengthen) - individualize
Watch for radiographic progression or new enhancement (possible transformation)
Neurocognitive and seizure follow-up
A confirmed progression enters the recurrence pathway

nodes.name: HGG surveillance
nodes.title: High-grade glioma / GBM surveillance
nodes.description: Closer MRI surveillance with awareness of pseudoprogression early after chemoradiation.
bullets: MRI roughly every 2-4 months (individualize) after completing chemoradiation
Distinguish pseudoprogression (early post-chemoradiation) from true progression - short-interval re-imaging / perfusion helps
Monitor steroid needs and performance status
A confirmed progression enters the recurrence pathway

nodes.name: Recurrence type
nodes.title: Recurrence: tumor category
nodes.description: At recurrence, first confirm true progression (versus pseudoprogression / treatment effect), then select the category to guide salvage options.
bullets: Confirm true progression on MRI (+/- perfusion / spectroscopy or biopsy)
Re-review molecular class and prior therapy received

nodes.name: Recurrent LGG
nodes.title: Recurrent lower-grade glioma: re-resection / deferred modality
nodes.description: Salvage for recurrent lower-grade glioma uses whichever modality has not yet been given, often after re-resection to confirm grade (watch for transformation).
bullets: Re-resection where feasible (confirms grade; rules out transformation to higher grade)
Radiation if not previously given; chemotherapy (temozolomide or PCV) if radiation already delivered
If transformed to grade 4, treat on the high-grade pathway
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges any systemic regimen (guidance only, no dose here)

nodes.name: Recurrent astro G4
nodes.title: Recurrent grade 4 IDH-mut astrocytoma: salvage
nodes.description: Salvage mirrors recurrent glioblastoma - re-resection, re-irradiation, and alkylator-based systemic therapy, with generally better outcomes than IDH-wildtype disease.
bullets: Re-resection for accessible, symptomatic recurrence
Re-irradiation in selected cases
Alkylator-based systemic therapy (temozolomide rechallenge or lomustine); clinical trial encouraged
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the regimen (guidance only, no dose here)

nodes.name: Recurrent GBM resectable
nodes.title: Recurrent glioblastoma: resectability
nodes.description: For recurrent glioblastoma, whether the recurrence is safely resectable steers toward re-operation versus systemic therapy / re-irradiation.

nodes.name: Recurrent GBM surgery
nodes.title: Recurrent GBM, resectable: re-resection then systemic
nodes.description: A focal, symptomatic, safely resectable glioblastoma recurrence is re-operated, optionally with local therapy, followed by systemic treatment.
bullets: Re-resection for symptomatic mass effect / focal recurrence
Consider a locally implanted carmustine wafer at re-operation in selected cases
Follow with systemic therapy (bevacizumab, lomustine, or temozolomide rechallenge) and/or re-irradiation
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the regimen (guidance only, no dose here); clinical trial encouraged

nodes.name: Recurrent GBM systemic
nodes.title: Recurrent GBM, unresectable: systemic / re-irradiation
nodes.description: Diffuse or unresectable glioblastoma recurrence is managed with systemic therapy and/or re-irradiation, prioritizing a clinical trial where available.
bullets: Systemic options: bevacizumab (helps edema / symptoms), lomustine, or temozolomide rechallenge (esp. MGMT-methylated with a treatment-free interval)
Re-irradiation for focal recurrence in selected patients
Best supportive care for poor performance status
No CNS dose protocol in library yet - physician arranges the regimen (guidance only, no dose here); clinical trial encouraged
